READ · SESSION 1

Living things

Look around: some things are living and some are not.

Living things share some important characteristics.

  • They perform the three vital functions.
  • They are born, grow and die.
  • They need water and nutrients.
🎯 Quick check: Which one is living?
OBSERVE

The three vital functions

All living things perform nutrition, reproduction and interaction.

🍎 Nutrition
🐣 Reproduction
👀 Interaction
🧠 Which list has the three vital functions?
THINK

Born, grow and die

Living things change during their lives and need water and nutrients.

A living thing is born, grows and dies.

Living things also need water and nutrients.

🌱 A plant grows and needs water. What does this tell us?
ANSWER

Living or non-living?

Use what you know to classify the examples from the book.

Which picture shows living things?

🎮 Then classify the book examples
READ

Living things are made of cells

A cell is a small unit that makes up a living thing.

Living things are made up of one or more small units called cells.

🔬 What are living things made of?
OBSERVE

Unicellular or multicellular?

Some living things have one cell. Others have many cells.

Unicellular

They have one cell. Algae and bacteria are unicellular organisms.

Multicellular

They have many cells. Plants, animals and fungi are multicellular organisms.

⚡ Which group has many cells?
